Playbook.name: FortiGate — Horizontal Network Sweep (Host Discovery) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One internal source was denied connections to 300+ distinct destinations in an hour - a horizontal sweep mapping live hosts. Triage question: is an internal host performing reconnaissance (possible compromise or rogue scanner), or is it an approved vulnerability scanner?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Internal host discovery is an early lateral-movement / recon step; from a non-scanner host it can indicate a compromised machine mapping the network.

Assets.AssetType: FortiGate perimeter and internal firewalls (HQ + DR)
Internal server and user segments behind the FortiGate

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FortiGate logs shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-fortinet_fortigate.* (verified live).

Fields: fortinet.firewall.subtype (ips/dns/...), fortinet.firewall.action, fortinet.firewall.severity, fortinet.firewall.attack, fortinet.firewall.srccountry/dstcountry ('Reserved' = RFC1918 internal), fortinet.firewall.cfgpath, dns.question.name, source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port.

Signal.Name: Horizontal sweep
Signal.Details: internal source, action deny, cardinality(destination.ip) >= 300; known scanners excluded.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Approved scanners (Nessus 192.168.166.1) are excluded; any OTHER internal host sweeping hundreds of destinations is treated as recon until identified.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the sweeping host is an approved scanner or an unexpected/compromised internal host, and whether it also succeeded in reaching hosts.

Step.name: Sweep breadth, ports and denied/accepted split
Step.Purpose: Characterise the sweep: how many destinations, which ports, and crucially whether any connections were ACCEPTED (not just denied).
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.traffic-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS total = COUNT(*), dsts = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), denied = COUNT(CASE(fortinet.firewall.action == "deny", 1, null)), accepted = COUNT(CASE(fortinet.firewall.action == "accept", 1, null)), dports = VALUES(destination.port) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many distinct destinations on a few ports = sweep. accepted > 0 means the host reached some targets - pivot to what it did there. A single scanned port (e.g. 445) across the estate = SMB discovery for lateral movement.

Step.name: What is this source and does it normally scan
Step.Purpose: Profile the source's overall behavior to separate a scanner/monitoring host from a workstation that should never sweep.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.traffic-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS conns = COUNT(*), dstcountries = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.dstcountry), top_ports = VALUES(destination.port) BY fortinet.firewall.action | SORT conns DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A workstation IP (user segment) sweeping is high concern; a monitoring/management host may do this legitimately. Correlate the IP with its segment/role.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the sweep included ACCEPTED connections (the host reached targets), especially on 445/135/3389.
Node.Result: True Positive (Internal Recon with Reach - escalate, treat source as possibly compromised)

Node.Condition: INV-01/02 show a broad sweep from a user-segment host that is not an approved scanner.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unauthorised Internal Scanning - investigate the host)

Node.Condition: Source is an approved scanner/monitoring host that was not in the exclusion list.
Sweep from a server whose role is unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FGSWEEP-SHAPE, INV-02-FGSWEEP-SRC to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: An approved vulnerability scanner or network-monitoring host.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the scanner; add to the rule exclusion; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: An internal host performing host-discovery recon (possible compromise or rogue tool).

Indicators.Item: Broad sweep from a non-scanner host.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate/triage the source host; hunt for the scanning process.
Check what accepted connections reached; open IR if compromise indicators.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured application/monitoring job scanning broadly by accident.

Indicators.Item: A known app/monitoring host due to a broken config.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the job; document and exclude if appropriate.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the source host and its role.
If accepted connections on lateral ports: isolate and triage.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Forensic triage of the host; scope what it reached; hunt lateral movement.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Segment user/workstation networks; restrict east-west; alert on non-scanner sweeps.

QualityChecks.Check: Rule excludes known scanners; threshold 300 destinations/hr. 'Reserved' srccountry = internal.
The accepted-connection split (INV-01) is the key escalation discriminator.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Approved scanner confirmed; deny-only; documented and excluded.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Source host triaged; reach scoped; no compromise or fully eradicated.
